document.cue: Describe a skill you learned that is useful for work.

text: I'd like to talk about public speaking, a skill that I started to develop about three years ago. Back then, I was extremely shy and would panic whenever I had to speak in front of more than three people, which was a real obstacle, since I had just started working part-time as a tutor.

To overcome it, I joined a small speaking club that met every Thursday evening. The format was simple: each member gave a short talk, and then we received constructive feedback from the group. At first I could hardly finish a sentence, but gradually I learned to structure my ideas, control my breathing and make eye contact. I also watched a lot of talks by experienced speakers online and tried to copy some of their techniques, such as pausing before an important point. Within a year, I was comfortable enough to deliver a ten-minute presentation to a large audience.

I use it almost every day, whether it's explaining a topic to students, presenting ideas in meetings or simply persuading someone to see my point of view. It's useful because, no matter how good your ideas are, they won't have much impact if you can't communicate them clearly. It has also boosted my confidence in general, which has helped me in job interviews and in networking. I'd say it's one of the best investments I've ever made in myself, and I'd encourage anyone to try it.

tips.en: Would + whenever describes a repeated past reaction.
tips.kk: Would + whenever өткендегі қайталанатын реакцияны сипаттайды.
